source.title: Leak-Resistant Unlearning: A New Benchmark for Evaluating Multi-Hop Reasoning Consistency and Recovery Robustness
source.authors: Haoting Qian; Qingjie Zhang; Zhi-Cong Huang; Cheng Hong; Han Qiu

record.tranche_reason: Applies named recovery attacks and reports recovery rates on new benchmark questions and models.
record.gate_note: Table 3 directly measures recovery after unlearning. Table 2 also reports forget quality across reasoning paths, but its many separate results are not extracted here because of the row limit. The selected Table 3 rows prioritize coverage of every model and unlearning method for FocusOnKey and quantization, plus selected multi-hop conditions and a small Probab sample.
record.test_reason: Applies existing recovery attacks (multinomial sampling, FocusOnKey key-token repetition, INT4 quantization) to six unlearning methods on three new models and newly curated multi-hop data. It reports Recovery Rate on unlearned items (Table 3) and forget quality across reasoning paths (Table 2).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude existing methods leak unlearned knowledge through alternative multi-hop reasoning paths and remain easily recoverable by simple attacks, often more so for multi-hop than single-hop queries. They add that no method jointly achieves forget quality, robustness and utility.
record.recipe_differences: The study implements six established unlearning methods and tunes hyperparameters separately for each method-model combination; it evaluates them on its own curated benchmark rather than reporting an explicit replication.
record.method_sensitivity: Recovery varies by model, unlearning method, attack, and single-hop versus multi-hop query. The authors also report that forgetting quality varies across reasoning structures.
record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The authors note reliance on LLM-generated and LLM-judged data, limited coverage of 3 models, 6 methods, 3 recovery methods, and 2 datasets, and an English-focused factual-knowledge scope. Recovery-rate uncertainty estimates are not reported in the displayed results.
record.rows_left_out: At the 60-row limit, the extraction omits most Probab conditions from Table 3, including other unlearning methods, and omits unselected multi-hop conditions for FocusOnKey and quantization. The many Table 2 forget-quality results across models, methods, and reasoning types are also not extracted.

untested.parts: No relearning or fine-tuning attack is run.
No activation-direction ablation or internal analysis.
Only INT4 is tested; no other bit widths or quantization schemes.

Jailbreaks, other languages and in-context information are not tested (the authors list cross-lingual leakage as future work). Rephrasing is covered only through the Table 2 multi-hop forget-quality results.
No method is presented or tested as a robust counter-method. PALU and AS are newer methods but are not claimed to resist these attacks.

missing.what: Probab recovery rates for NPO, TV, PALU, RMU and AS on all models. Notably 90.8 for AS on Qwen3-32B, which resists the other two attacks, and 4.0/5.9 for PALU on Llama.
Remaining FocusOnKey and INT4 multi-hop values (e.g. GA Llama FoK MH 62.5, GA Qwen3-32B INT4 MH 85.7).
Forget quality on multi-hop reformulations without any attack. Negative FQ means accuracy rose after unlearning, e.g. AS Llama MT -43.9 and MP -54.8, PALU Llama MP -26.0.
Utility (BBH) trade-off, e.g. PALU on Llama reduces BBH to 49.9% while RMU keeps 99.2%.

record.verdict_notes: Recovery Rate is computed over successfully unlearned items, so the implicit baseline is 0. Row states describe the size of the recovery effect. For A, observed recovery counts against A. FocusOnKey's original paper (Zhang et al. 2025a) shares authors with this study, so E evidence from FoK is partly by its own originators. Quantization is INT4 per Table 5. Correctness is judged by an LLM judge that counts any occurrence of the ground truth as correct, which may inflate recovery. No uncertainty is reported. Datasets (MQuAKE vs Books) are not separated in Table 3. Methods were tuned per model, with no near-chance check reported.

versions.untested_parts: The extracted rows measure recovery attacks; they do not jointly establish near-chance targeted accuracy and preserved general ability for each attack condition.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning on unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten-fact examples.
No activation-direction ablation or direct internal analysis showing access blocking rather than deletion.
The extracted results cover quantization recovery; other bit widths are not stated as tested.
FocusOnKey repeats key tokens. Rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, and in-context information are not tested.
The evaluated methods are tested against the included recovery attacks; resistance to fine-tuning or activation ablation is not tested.

relation.reason: Reports recovery rates after unlearning under three attacks.

tranche.reason: Applies existing recovery attacks to new models and a new multi-hop benchmark and reports results on the claim. It is not the original method or measure, so T3, not T1.

source_check.notes: Table 3 does not say whether its values come from MQuAKE or Books. FocusOnKey (Zhang et al. 2025a, arXiv:2509.24675) shares five authors with this study, so the FoK results come from the attack's own group. In Table 3, Llama RMU FoK SH equals Quant SH (59.2) and Probab MH equals Quant MH (76.3), which may be a copying quirk. Hyperparameters were tuned per (method, model), and an LLM judges correctness.

statements.problem: Makes no claim about this study.

statements.correction: Qwen INT4 supporting rows: Qwen3-14B GA 79.7, NPO 82.1, TV 66.4, PALU 51.2, AS 79.0 (SH); Qwen3-32B GA 77.7, NPO 86.9, TV 56.8 (SH); Qwen3-14B PALU 61.6, AS 86.5 (MH) (R31-R34, R36-R39, R45, R46).
statements.problem: Minor: the remark that Qwen supporting rows are 'not shown in the pack' is out of date. The Qwen INT4 rows exist and the statement cites them.

statements.correction: Datasets: curated multi-hop sets from MQuAKE and Books (MUSE Harry Potter corpus); Table 3 dataset not stated.
statements.problem: Minor: one of the study's two datasets (Books) is built on MUSE's Harry Potter books (Shi et al., 2024), and Table 3 does not say which dataset its values come from. 'Not from MUSE' is right only in the sense of not using the MUSE benchmark's own metrics.

statements.correction: INT4 SH by model (Llama-3.1-8B / Qwen3-14B / Qwen3-32B): GA 85.7 / 79.7 / 77.7; AS 55.9 / 79.0 / 0.0; PALU 4.0 / 51.2 / 0.0 (Table 3). Same-method contrasts: AS or PALU, Qwen3-14B vs Qwen3-32B.
statements.problem: The numbers are right, but the example changes method and model at once (GA on Llama vs PALU/AS on Qwen3-32B), so it can't show a model family or scale effect. GA hardly varies by model.
The range 51.9-95.0 does not cover Qwen3-14B PALU single-hop (FoK 41.2), one of the cells the statement names. Only its MH value, 56.0, is in range.

statements.correction: FoK SH/MH: RMU Llama 59.2/59.6, Qwen3-14B 35.5/23.2, Qwen3-32B 28.9/38.8; GA Qwen3-14B 8.6/11.2; AS Qwen3-32B 0.0/0.0; PALU Llama 0.9/2.4 (Table 3).
statements.problem: Puts RMU in the 2.4-41.2% group without naming the model. On Llama, FoK recovers 59.2 SH / 59.6 MH for RMU, and E.support[2] lists that cell as strong recovery. The range fits RMU only on the Qwen models. It also leaves out the low GA cell on Qwen3-14B.

statements.correction: If the study is meant here, the same-model method contrast is Qwen3-32B FoK SH: GA 95.0 vs AS 0.0 (Table 3).
statements.problem: Cites R01 and R18 from this study, but the text says nothing about it. R01 (Llama GA) and R18 (Qwen3-32B AS) also differ in model as well as method.
Makes no claim about this study.
